xaEvsBHmC7c.speaker: adnan
xaEvsBHmC7c.speaker_note: regular Ramadan Quranic Reflections voice; a guest speaker briefly takes the microphone from about 42:10
xaEvsBHmC7c.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 21: Quranic Reflections on Al-Ahzab 35 to Ya-Sin 54
xaEvsBHmC7c.one_line: Obedience when it is hard: no option after Allah decrees, wealth as test, dignity from Allah, the miser's argument, and entering the last ten nights.
xaEvsBHmC7c.summary: He introduces the sixth cluster of surahs, on obedience to Allah specifically when it is hard: Saba treats a community's obedience, Fatir obedience grounded in knowledge, and Ya-Sin obedience as the source of true life of the spirit. Al-Ahzab 36, which he calls the cluster's central verse, says a believer has no option once Allah and His Messenger decree; he challenges young Muslims who say 'it's my choice' or are 'maturing a decision', while insisting no one may force religion on anyone. Saba 37 teaches that wealth and children, symbols of financial and social strength, bring no one closer to Allah unless joined to faith and good deeds, and that abundance is a test, not a sign of love. Fatir 10 says all dignity belongs to Allah: those who seek it through coercion and plotting, like Pharaoh, end cursed. Ya-Sin 47 exposes the argument 'why feed those Allah could feed?'; starvation, he says, proves people withhold what Allah placed in their hands for others. Entering the last ten nights, he describes the Prophet's intensified worship, the hidden timing of Laylat al-Qadr, and urges everyone to forgive and seek forgiveness, since the night's timing was lost because of a dispute.

outline.heading: Opening
Sixth cluster: obedience when it is hard
outline.gist: The cluster from Al-Ahzab looks at submission from different angles, each surah focused on obeying when it is difficult, physically, spiritually, psychologically, socially or reputationally. That is where true colours show and where Allah grants enlightenment to those who hold their ground.

outline.heading: Saba: a community's obedience
outline.gist: Unlike the rest of the cluster, which addresses the individual, Saba deals with how a whole community submits to Allah, which takes a different form.

outline.heading: Fatir: obedience through knowledge
outline.gist: We obey Allah the way He wants, not the way we want, which requires knowledge, clarity and certainty; that makes obedience decisive and gives a life of dignity.

outline.heading: Ya-Sin: obedience as true life
outline.gist: Obeying Allah gives the life of the spirit, not just the body, and a legacy can outlive your years. He suggests early Muslims recited Ya-Sin for the dead because they grasped this theme, though there may be no authentic evidence for the practice.

outline.heading: Interlude
The central verse: no option after a decree
outline.gist: In his view the central verse of the whole cluster: when Allah and His Messenger decide a matter, a believing man or woman has no choice left in it.

outline.heading: Easy or hard, a Muslim obeys
outline.gist: Once something is declared obligatory or forbidden, it is no longer optional, whether it suits you or is extremely difficult.

outline.heading: 'It's my choice'
outline.gist: Younger Muslims often defend their practice as their choice; he asks what they mean by it.

outline.heading: Interlude
No one may force you, but a believer does not deliberate
outline.gist: If it means no one should force you, he agrees. But for a true believer, once Allah says something is obligatory it is not a choice; it follows automatically.

outline.heading: Freedom of religion versus playing with words
outline.gist: Islam completely rejects forcing anyone into a religion. The problem is using 'my choice' to imply every command is optional.

outline.heading: 'Maturing my decision'
outline.gist: Phrases like 'maturing my decision' baffle him. If you believe in Allah and He said do this, the logic is linear and simple; the word 'choice' should be used more carefully.

outline.heading: How a believer should internalise commands
outline.gist: Whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has gone clearly astray. It is not his role to force or judge others; he describes how a believer should feel on hearing a command: immediate acceptance is the hallmark of true faith.

outline.heading: Not wealth or children that bring you near
outline.gist: Saba addresses communities' obedience. Zulfa means being drawn close: neither your money nor your children bring you closer to Allah, but your beliefs, intentions and deeds.

outline.heading: A multiplied reward in safe chambers
outline.gist: Those who believe and do good receive a reward multiplied many times and dwell secure in the high rooms of Paradise.

outline.heading: Like the sacrifice: only taqwa reaches Him
outline.gist: Just as the meat and blood of sacrifices do not reach Allah but the taqwa in hearts does, status, power and riches mean nothing; only faith internalised and turned into commanded deeds draws you near.

outline.heading: Wealth and children as symbols of strength
outline.gist: In the Quran wealth and children stand for financial and social strength, just as the poor and the orphan symbolise financial and social disadvantage. Many children once meant protection and people to vouch for you.

outline.heading: Except those who believe and do good
outline.gist: None of it matters to Allah on its own. The phrasing means that once you have faith and righteous deeds, your wealth and social standing start bringing you closer; without them they mean nothing.

outline.heading: Abundance is a test, not a sign of love
outline.gist: People misread wealth and status as Allah's approval. He tests some with plenty and some with little, with ease and with difficulty; that is all it is.

outline.heading: The poor companions and the dhikr after prayer
outline.gist: Poor companions complained that the wealthy took all the reward through their spending. The Prophet taught them words of remembrance after prayer, the rich learned it and did the same, and he said this is Allah's bounty given to whom He wills.

outline.heading: A double-edged sword
outline.gist: Wealth and status can bring heavy accountability and collapse under the responsibility, or lift you to the highest places in Paradise; with great power comes great responsibility. Used for Allah, they earn a doubled reward.

outline.heading: Allah is never obeyed through ignorance
outline.gist: Fatir corrects misconceptions so that we obey according to His will, not ours. He chooses how He is worshipped; we cannot invent forms of worship He never asked for.

outline.heading: The man who stood in the sun
outline.gist: A companion vowed to stand in the sun, refuse shade, stay silent and fast. The Prophet told him to sit, take shade and speak, and to complete only his fast, because Allah loves to be worshipped through fasting, not made-up hardships.

outline.heading: All dignity belongs to Allah
outline.gist: Whoever wants honour must seek it from its source, Allah, who alone grants it. Seeking it through people or other means gives something temporary that soon wears off.

outline.heading: Pharaoh's borrowed dignity
outline.gist: Pharaoh sought honour through authority and coercion, boasting of the rivers flowing beneath him, until the sea closed over him; to this day his name is cursed. Good words ascend to Allah and righteous deeds raise them.

outline.heading: Interlude
Plotting for status comes to nothing
outline.gist: Those who scheme evil in power struggles to get ahead will face severe punishment, and their plotting will amount to nothing. Status gained that way lasts only a few years.

outline.heading: The Prophet's lasting honour
outline.gist: He had little wealth, few children and was persecuted for most of his life, yet people send blessings on him every day, because dignity is granted and taken by Allah.

outline.heading: Ya-Sin: the life of the spirit
outline.gist: Obeying Allah's law grants the long-term life that continues after the body stops, the real life worth seeking.

outline.heading: 'Why feed those Allah could feed?'
outline.gist: Told to spend, the disbelievers ask why they should feed someone Allah could have fed Himself, and accuse the believers of being astray. The argument is recorded so we never make it.

outline.heading: Provision placed in other people's hands
outline.gist: People do not starve because Allah fails to provide. He placed part of their provision in others' hands, obliging them to give, and they did not.

outline.heading: Starvation is evidence of misused wealth
outline.gist: The starving will find justice and those who withheld aid will answer for it. Allah tests the poor with hardship and the wealthy with ease, giving them more so they can give.

outline.heading: Do you think it was all your own doing?
outline.gist: People work hard for their wealth, but believing it came only from your intelligence is delusional; your project could have failed a million times.

outline.heading: When the spirit dies, the mouth says this
outline.gist: Refusing to give to someone because Allah did not give to them is the epitome of evil. Whatever extra you have, whether time, expertise, compassion or wealth, is there for those without enough, and you will be asked about it.

outline.heading: Interlude
A community gathered around the Quran
outline.gist: A community gathered around the Book of Allah will be strong and find its way through difficulty. Youth should carry the Quran by understanding and practising it, and start memorising while the brain is a sponge.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Prophet's effort in the last ten nights
outline.gist: He stayed awake most or all of the night and woke his family, not letting Aisha sleep as she did earlier in the month, and worked harder than at any other time.

outline.heading: Why Allah hid Laylat al-Qadr
outline.gist: Fatigue sets in, but this is the time to renew intention. Allah hides the night as He hides which deed carries most weight and which name He answers by, so that we strive in all of them.

outline.heading: Dedicate all ten nights
outline.gist: Despite cultural love for the twenty-seventh, no one knows the night; some scholars even hold it may differ from person to person. Devote all ten nights and you will surely catch it.

outline.heading: Interlude
Review your relationships and forgive
outline.gist: Muslims historically cleared their hearts at the start of the last ten nights: forgive anyone you hold something against and seek forgiveness from those who hold something against you, relatives and friends included.

outline.heading: The night's date lost to a dispute
outline.gist: The Prophet came out to tell them the date and found two men arguing; by the time he settled it he had forgotten. The story is symbolic, since Jibril could have told him again. Seek it in the odd nights of the last ten.

outline.heading: Tonight could be the night
outline.gist: Abu Said saw the Prophet with mud on his forehead on the twenty-first, when rain fell on the uncarpeted masjid, so the very first night may be it.

outline.heading: Be as tame as a sheep
outline.gist: Scholars inferred that if the Prophet lost the night's timing through a dispute, a servant can lose its blessing the same way. Avoid arguments, let go of your ego and forgive.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: The sixth cluster is about obeying Allah precisely when it is hard.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: Saba deals with a community's collective obedience, which differs from an individual's.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Obedience gives the true life of the spirit and a legacy that outlives the body.

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: Once Allah and His Messenger decree, a believer has no option; 'it's my choice' cannot mean commands are optional, though no one may force religion.

themes.label: Freedom, rights and responsibility
themes.note: Freedom of religion means no coercion, not that obligations become optional for believers.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Wealth and children bring no one closer to Allah on their own; abundance is a test that can raise or ruin you.

themes.label: Extremism, bad religiosity and distorted practice
themes.note: Allah is obeyed through knowledge, not invented hardships, as the man standing in the sun was taught.

themes.label: Self-value, self-worth, confidence
themes.note: All dignity belongs to Allah; seeking it through coercion or plotting ends in disgrace, while the Prophet's honour endures.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: People starve because others withhold what Allah placed in their hands; any surplus is meant for those in need.

themes.label: Selfishness, greed of the soul (shuhh) and selflessness
themes.note: Believing your wealth is all your own doing, and refusing to give, is a sign of a dead spirit.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: The Prophet's intensified worship in the last ten nights and why Laylat al-Qadr is hidden.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: Clear disputes at the start of the last ten nights, since the night's timing was lost through a quarrel.

quran.point: Not the meat or blood of sacrifices reaches Allah, but taqwa: the same principle as wealth and children.
Pharaoh boasting of the rivers flowing beneath him as his claim to honour.

hadith.gist: Poor companions said the wealthy had taken all the reward; the Prophet taught them remembrance after prayer, the wealthy did the same, and he said it is Allah's bounty He gives to whom He wills.
A man vowed to stand in the sun, not sit, not take shade, not speak and fast; the Prophet told him to sit, take shade and speak, and complete his fast.
In the last ten nights the Prophet stayed up the night and woke his family.
The Prophet came out to tell the date of Laylat al-Qadr, found two men disputing, and its knowledge was taken away; seek it in the odd nights of the last ten.
Abu Said saw the Prophet with traces of water and mud on his forehead after prostrating on the morning of the twenty-first.

maxims: True believers don't feel they have options
Allah is never obeyed through ignorance
All dignity belongs to Allah
Starvation is evidence people aren't using wealth as commanded
Your extra is there so you can give it
Be as tame as a sheep in these nights

stories.who: The poor companions and the dhikr after prayer
stories.point: Wealth used for Allah can raise a person, and Allah's bounty is His to give.

stories.who: Abu Israil standing in the sun
stories.point: Allah is worshipped as He wants, not through self-invented hardship.

stories.who: Pharaoh
stories.point: Honour sought through coercion ends in a name cursed for ever.

stories.who: The two men whose dispute erased the date of Laylat al-Qadr
stories.point: Quarrels cost blessings; forgive and let go of ego in the last ten nights.

contemporary: Young Muslims describing religious obligations as 'my choice' or as 'maturing a decision'
Starvation in the world as the result of withheld wealth
takeaways: When Allah and His Messenger have ruled on something, treat it as settled, without forcing or judging others.
Do not read wealth or status as a sign of Allah's love; use them for His sake.
Learn how Allah wants to be worshipped instead of inventing your own practices.
Give from whatever you have beyond your needs: wealth, time, expertise and compassion.
In the last ten nights, renew your intention, strive every night, and forgive and seek forgiveness to clear disputes.

36:78.ar: وَضَرَبَ لَنَا مَثَلࣰ ا وَنَسِيَ خَلۡقَهُۥۖ قَالَ مَن يُحۡيِ ٱلۡعِظَٰمَ وَهِيَ رَمِيمࣱ‏
36:78.en: And he presents for Us an example and forgets his [own] creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are disintegrated

36:79.ar: قُلۡ يُحۡيِيهَا ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنشَأَهَآ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةࣲۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ خَلۡقٍ عَلِيمٌ
36:79.en: Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time; and He is, of all creation, Knowing

37:62.ar: أَذَٰلِكَ خَيۡرࣱ نُّزُلًا أَمۡ شَجَرَةُ ٱلزَّقُّومِ
37:62.en: Is Paradise a better accommodation or the tree of zaqqum

37:63.en: Indeed, We have made it a torment for the wrongdoers

37:64.ar: إِنَّهَا شَجَرَةࣱ تَخۡرُجُ فِيٓ أَصۡلِ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
37:64.en: Indeed, it is a tree issuing from the bottom of the Hellfire

37:65.en: Its emerging fruit as if it was heads of the devils

37:66.ar: فَإِنَّهُمۡ لَأٓكِلُونَ مِنۡهَا فَمَالِـُٔونَ مِنۡهَا ٱلۡبُطُونَ
37:66.en: And indeed, they will eat from it and fill with it their bellies

37:67.ar: ثُمَّ إِنَّ لَهُمۡ عَلَيۡهَا لَشَوۡبࣰ ا مِّنۡ حَمِيمࣲ‏
37:67.en: Then indeed, they will have after it a mixture of scalding water

37:68.en: Then indeed, their return will be to the Hellfire

37:69.en: Indeed they found their fathers astray

37:70.en: So they hastened [to follow] in their footsteps

37:102.ar: فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعۡيَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَيَّ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰ فِي ٱلۡمَنَامِ أَنِّيٓ أَذۡبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرۡ مَاذَا تَرَىٰۚ قَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفۡعَلۡ مَا تُؤۡمَرُۖ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
37:102.en: And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion, he said, "O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I [must] sacrifice you, so see what you think." He said, "O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, of the steadfast

37:103.en: And when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead

37:105.ar: قَدۡ صَدَّقۡتَ ٱلرُّءۡيَآۚ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
37:105.en: You have fulfilled the vision." Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good

37:106.en: Indeed, this was the clear trial

37:107.en: And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice

38:41.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ عَبۡدَنَآ أَيُّوبَ إِذۡ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ بِنُصۡبࣲ وَعَذَابٍ
38:41.en: And remember Our servant Job, when he called to his Lord, "Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment

38:42.ar: ٱرۡكُضۡ بِرِجۡلِكَۖ هَٰذَا مُغۡتَسَلُۢ بَارِدࣱ وَشَرَابࣱ‏
38:42.en: [So he was told], "Strike [the ground] with your foot; this is a [spring for] a cool bath and drink

38:43.ar: وَوَهَبۡنَا لَهُۥٓ أَهۡلَهُۥ وَمِثۡلَهُم مَّعَهُمۡ رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّنَّا وَذِكۡرَىٰ لِأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
38:43.en: And We granted him his family and a like [number] with them as mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding

38:44.ar: وَخُذۡ بِيَدِكَ ضِغۡثࣰ ا فَٱضۡرِب بِّهِۦ وَلَا تَحۡنَثۡۗ إِنَّا وَجَدۡنَٰهُ صَابِرࣰ اۚ نِّعۡمَ ٱلۡعَبۡدُ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابࣱ‏
38:44.en: [We said], "And take in your hand a bunch [of grass] and strike with it and do not break your oath." Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one repeatedly turning back [to Allah]

39:9.ar: أَمَّنۡ هُوَ قَٰنِتٌ ءَانَآءَ ٱلَّيۡلِ سَاجِدࣰ ا وَقَآئِمࣰ ا يَحۡذَرُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَ وَيَرۡجُواْ رَحۡمَةَ رَبِّهِۦۗ قُلۡ هَلۡ يَسۡتَوِي ٱلَّذِينَ يَعۡلَمُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَۗ إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
39:9.en: Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing [in prayer], fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, [like one who does not]? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" Only they will remember [who are] people of understanding

39:42.ar: ٱللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى ٱلۡأَنفُسَ حِينَ مَوۡتِهَا وَٱلَّتِي لَمۡ تَمُتۡ فِي مَنَامِهَاۖ فَيُمۡسِكُ ٱلَّتِي قَضَىٰ عَلَيۡهَا ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَيُرۡسِلُ ٱلۡأُخۡرَىٰٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ مُّسَمًّىۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
39:42.en: Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die [He takes] during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others for a specified term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought

96:1.en: Recite in the name of your Lord who created

2:260.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيۡفَ تُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِنۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَئِنَّ قَلۡبِيۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ جُزۡءࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيࣰ اۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
2:260.en: And [mention] when Abraham said, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." [Allah] said, "Have you not believed?" He said, "Yes, but [I ask] only that my heart may be satisfied." [Allah] said, "Take four birds and commit them to yourself. Then [after slaughtering them] put on each hill a portion of them; then call them - they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise

33:36.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنࣲ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:36.en: It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should [thereafter] have any choice about their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error

4:34.ar: ٱلرِّجَالُ قَوَّٰمُونَ عَلَى ٱلنِّسَآءِ بِمَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡضَهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ وَبِمَآ أَنفَقُواْ مِنۡ أَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡۚ فَٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ قَٰنِتَٰتٌ حَٰفِظَٰتࣱ لِّلۡغَيۡبِ بِمَا حَفِظَ ٱللَّهُۚ وَٱلَّٰتِي تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ فَعِظُوهُنَّ وَٱهۡجُرُوهُنَّ فِي ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ وَٱضۡرِبُوهُنَّۖ فَإِنۡ أَطَعۡنَكُمۡ فَلَا تَبۡغُواْ عَلَيۡهِنَّ سَبِيلًاۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيࣰّ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
4:34.en: Men are in charge of women by [right of] what Allah has given one over the other and what they spend [for maintenance] from their wealth. So righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in [the husband's] absence what Allah would have them guard. But those [wives] from whom you fear arrogance - [first] advise them; [then if they persist], forsake them in bed; and [finally], strike them. But if they obey you [once more], seek no means against them. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Grand

32:9.ar: ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰهُ وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِهِۦۖ وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرَ وَٱلۡأَفۡـِٔدَةَۚ قَلِيلࣰ ا مَّا تَشۡكُرُونَ
32:9.en: Then He proportioned him and breathed into him from His [created] soul and made for you hearing and vision and hearts; little are you grateful

LGPvmawj3Tc.speaker: adnan
LGPvmawj3Tc.speaker_note: Ramadan 2024 Quranic Reflections series he leads; speaks of his own years as an imam in Syria
LGPvmawj3Tc.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 22: Quranic Reflections (Ya-Sin 55 to Az-Zumar 61)
LGPvmawj3Tc.one_line: Closing the obedience cluster: resurrection and contemplation, blind tradition, Ibrahim's sacrifice, Ayyub's quick return, sincerity, and sleep as the soul's nightly return.
LGPvmawj3Tc.summary: He frames al-Ahzab through az-Zumar as one cluster on obedience to Allah seen from several angles: obeying when it is hard, obedience of a whole society, obedience grounded in knowledge, obedience as the route to true life, obeying commands whose wisdom you cannot see, returning quickly when you are wrong, and finally sincerity as the inner form of submission. From Ya-Sin he takes the man who crumbles an old bone and doubts resurrection, arguing that our own beginning was smaller and more fragile still, and that the denial came from never contemplating it. He laments that people no longer let ideas settle through long reflection. From as-Saffat he criticises following forefathers without scrutiny, insisting that inherited culture be sifted respectfully, as medicine does with Ibn Sina, and presents Ibrahim's readiness to sacrifice his son as the clearest test of obeying without explanation. From Sad he reads Ayyub's oath and the handful of grass as a prophet publicly owning a mistake, and clarifies that Islam never permitted wife beating or verbal abuse. From az-Zumar he explains the devoted, focused worshipper who is wary of the Hereafter, why the next life deserves more of our worry, and how sleep shows the soul's need to return to Allah, urging people to keep that connection alive while awake.

outline.heading: Opening
The obedience cluster; al-Ahzab: obeying when it is hard
outline.gist: The surahs from al-Ahzab to az-Zumar each treat submission to Allah from a different angle; al-Ahzab is about obeying when physical, social, financial or reputational costs make it difficult.

outline.heading: Saba: how a society obeys
outline.gist: The obedience of a community does not look like the obedience of an individual, and Saba is unique in addressing the collective.

outline.heading: Fatir: obeying through knowledge
outline.gist: Understanding His commands and His universe gives obedience integrity, clarity and meaning.

outline.heading: Ya-Sin: submission as the route to true life
outline.gist: Life is more than biology; obedience brings spiritual life and a legacy that continues after death, which is why Ya-Sin is traditionally read over graves.

outline.heading: As-Saffat: obeying what you do not understand
outline.gist: Every command carries benefit even when its wisdom is hidden from you or from where you are in life; explaining the wisdom of rulings is good, but making understanding a condition for obeying a clearly established command is not acceptable.

outline.heading: Sad: returning to the truth when you are wrong
outline.gist: Its stories show prophets who immediately admitted and repented of a mistake, ending with Iblis who kept going; admitting fault is hard because the ego fears for status, yet real submission requires it.

outline.heading: Az-Zumar: sincerity, the inner form of submission
outline.gist: After the outward, mechanical forms of obedience comes sincerity, which no one but Allah can see; it is the mother of the heart's good deeds, alongside humility and love that live inside and only show in behaviour.

outline.heading: The man who crumbled a bone
outline.gist: A man takes a decayed bone, crumbles it to dust and asks who could bring this back, forgetting his own creation.

outline.heading: Your beginning was smaller still
outline.gist: A fertilised egg is invisible and more fragile than dust; whoever brought you from that beginning can bring you back, yet we rarely internalise that this was our own start.

outline.heading: Contemplation: letting an idea brew
outline.gist: Contemplating means turning an idea over for weeks, arguing for and against until it matures; in a life of scrolling and quick lookups no one does this, and Allah deserves lifetimes of it.

outline.heading: Forgetting by refusing to think
outline.gist: The man knew his origin but chose not to dwell on it; the Quran repeatedly calls people of reason to reflect, and since learning only sinks in through repetition, the denial of resurrection came from a lack of contemplation.

outline.heading: Imams and verses ending in dallin
outline.gist: A drowsy congregation may answer Ameen when a verse ends in dallin, so the reciter should keep going; his own early years leading prayer in Syria taught him to adjust his pace and keep people engaged.

outline.heading: Those who found their fathers astray
outline.gist: Amid the description of the tree of Hell, Allah describes people who hurried along in the footsteps of misguided forefathers.

outline.heading: Two errors: change for its own sake and blind tradition
outline.gist: Some want change simply to change, others hold to tradition regardless of whether it is right or useful; the Quran condemns the idolaters who would not break with their fathers' legacy.

outline.heading: Our parents got some things right and some wrong
outline.gist: Offering a better way does not call your parents evil; even pre-Islamic Arabia had courage and generosity, so sift the inheritance, keep the good, adjust the rest and keep making dua for them.

outline.heading: Respecting Ibn Sina without practising like him
outline.gist: Copying the past without scrutiny is a heavy habit in the Muslim community; medicine honours Ibn Sina and keeps his principles while discarding what he got wrong, and we can do the same.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's command: the hardest test ever given
outline.gist: The story is told only once in the Quran: Ibrahim was told to slaughter his son with no reason or wisdom explained, the pinnacle of obeying without understanding.

outline.heading: The great debater who asked no questions
outline.gist: Ibrahim debated idol worshippers, a king, his people and his father, and even asked Allah to show him resurrection, yet when commanded to sacrifice his son he did not question; Ismail told him to do as he was commanded.

outline.heading: The knife that would not cut: the clear test
outline.gist: The knife did not cut and a ram was sent in his place; it never happened because Allah commands nothing without benefit, but Ibrahim had to show he would do it.

outline.heading: The Eid sacrifice as gratitude
outline.gist: We follow whether we see the reason or not, and celebrate by sacrificing an animal and feeding the poor, thankful that every command we were given is beneficial.

outline.heading: No choice once Allah has decided
outline.gist: Shaytan tried to turn Ibrahim, his wife and his son against the command, but a true believer does not see himself as having options when Allah and His Messenger command; he hears, obeys and moves on.

outline.heading: Ayyub: a prophet who lost everything
outline.gist: Sad tells of prophets who erred and returned quickly; Ayyub had wealth, status, prophethood, health and children, then lost it all and spent years ill and isolated while his wife cared for him.

outline.heading: The oath against his wife
outline.gist: When she asked why he did not pray for relief, he took it as objecting to Allah and swore to punish her, though she was already carrying more than she could bear and had not objected at all.

outline.heading: A handful of grass, and the one who turns back
outline.gist: Allah let him fulfil the oath harmlessly with a bunch of grass, exposing that his oath was wrong, and praised him as patient and quick to return.

outline.heading: What the discipline verse does and does not allow
outline.gist: The Quran's mention of physical discipline is narrowly reserved for infidelity that is destroying a marriage and never allows leaving a mark; wife beating and verbal abuse were never permitted and a wife could always take her husband to a judge.

outline.heading: Why the grass: making his mistake visible
outline.gist: Expiating quietly would have hidden his error from his wife; the grass let her see he was wrong, and all the prophets in Sad accepted blame without difficulty.

outline.heading: The devout one: focused on One
outline.gist: Az-Zumar is about sincerity; qanit means putting all your focus on one thing, which is why the witr supplication is called qunut, and here it describes the one who spends the night prostrating and standing.

outline.heading: Wary of the Hereafter
outline.gist: Without real worry about where you will stand on the Day of Judgment the practice of the deen eventually stops working; that worry, with hope for His mercy, must occupy most of your thought.

outline.heading: Are those who know equal to those who do not?
outline.gist: The night worshipper has understood what life is about and cannot be compared to those who do not know what is worth worrying about; only people of reason take heed.

outline.heading: Why worry about the Hereafter: it is longer
outline.gist: Eternity outlasts the few decades here, so on length alone it deserves more concern.

outline.heading: Why worry about the Hereafter: it is more intense
outline.gist: Paradise is better than any good here and Hell worse than any hardship.

outline.heading: Why worry about the Hereafter: a dedicated moment of accountability
outline.gist: Here you can get away with almost anything if no one catches you, but there is a set moment of open accountability.

outline.heading: Balance your worries and keep reassessing
outline.gist: Worrying about your worldly future is fine, but it should at least balance with the Hereafter; not knowing whether your deeds are accepted means constant self-assessment.

outline.heading: Sleep, the closest thing to death
outline.gist: Allah takes souls at death and also in sleep; dreamless sleep erases the sense of time, showing how relative time is.

outline.heading: Souls held back and souls sent back
outline.gist: Those decreed to die are kept with Him and the rest return until their appointed time; how this happens is beyond what he will speculate on.

outline.heading: Connect your spirit to Allah while awake
outline.gist: The spirit came from Allah and needs to return to Him every night to survive; the question is whether you revive that connection while you are awake and alive.

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: Seven angles on submission across al-Ahzab to az-Zumar, including obeying clear commands whose wisdom you cannot see.

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: Ibrahim's sacrifice as the clearest test of obeying without explanation; a believer has no option once Allah commands.

themes.label: Accepting the truth unconditionally vs stubbornness ('inad)
themes.note: Admitting a mistake quickly is central to real submission even though the ego fears losing status.

themes.label: Accepting the truth unconditionally vs stubbornness ('inad)
themes.note: Ayyub's oath and the handful of grass show a prophet openly accepting that he was wrong.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Sincerity is the inner mirror of submission, known only to Allah, and the mother of the heart's good deeds.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Resurrection is no harder than our invisible, fragile beginning.

themes.label: Contemplation and deep reflection (tafakkur)
themes.note: Real contemplation lets an idea brew for weeks; denial grows from refusing to think about what we already know.

themes.label: Blindly following forefathers and inherited tradition
themes.note: Sift what you inherit respectfully, keeping the good and letting go of the rest, as medicine does with Ibn Sina.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Ibrahim and Ismail at the sacrifice, and Ayyub's illness, oath and repentance.

themes.label: Marriage and the relationship between spouses
themes.note: Wife beating and verbal abuse were never permitted; the discipline verse is narrowly limited to infidelity.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Wariness of the Hereafter keeps the deen working; it is longer, more intense and has a dedicated moment of accountability.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: Sleep shows the spirit's need to return to Allah; keep that connection alive while awake.

quran.point: The first command given was to read and learn, part of the Quran's call to reflect.
Ibrahim asked Allah to show him how He gives life to the dead, showing he questioned everything except the sacrifice command.
A believer has no choice once Allah and His Messenger decide a matter.
The verse on physical discipline in marriage, which he limits narrowly and says never allowed beating.
Allah breathed into the human from His spirit, which is why the spirit must return to Him.

maxims: Sincerity is the mother of all good deeds of the heart
Cook the idea, marinate it, let it brew
Allah requires lifetimes of contemplation
A true believer sees no options when Allah commands
Letting go safely does not mean disrespecting those before us

stories.who: The man who crumbled a decayed bone and denied resurrection
stories.point: He forgot his own humble beginning because he never contemplated it.

stories.who: His early years leading prayer in Syria
stories.point: Mistakes taught him to adjust his pace and keep the congregation engaged.

stories.who: Ibn Sina
stories.point: We can honour a pioneer and keep his principles while discarding what he got wrong.

stories.who: Ibrahim and Ismail at the sacrifice
stories.point: The ultimate test of obeying a command with no explanation; a believer has no option once Allah commands.

stories.who: Ayyub, his wife and the handful of grass
stories.point: A prophet who recognised his oath was wrong and was shown a way to admit it openly without harm.

contemporary: Constant scrolling and quick online lookups crowding out reflection
A heavy habit in the Muslim community of copying the past without scrutiny
takeaways: Obey clearly established commands even when you cannot see their wisdom
Admit your mistakes quickly and accept the blame, as the prophets did
Sift inherited customs respectfully: keep the good, let go of the rest and keep making dua for your parents
Set aside real time to contemplate ideas, Allah and your own life
Let worry about the Hereafter at least balance worldly worries, and keep your spirit connected to Allah while awake

6:59.ar: ۞وَعِندَهُۥ مَفَاتِحُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ لَا يَعۡلَمُهَآ إِلَّا هُوَۚ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِۚ وَمَا تَسۡقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعۡلَمُهَا وَلَا حَبَّةࣲ فِي ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا رَطۡبࣲ وَلَا يَابِسٍ إِلَّا فِي كِتَٰبࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
6:59.en: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it. And no grain is there within the darknesses of the earth and no moist or dry [thing] but that it is [written] in a clear record

31:34.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عِندَهُۥ عِلۡمُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ وَيُنَزِّلُ ٱلۡغَيۡثَ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡحَامِۖ وَمَا تَدۡرِي نَفۡسࣱ مَّاذَا تَكۡسِبُ غَدࣰ اۖ وَمَا تَدۡرِي نَفۡسُۢ بِأَيِّ أَرۡضࣲ تَمُوتُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرُۢ
31:34.en: Indeed, Allah [alone] has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. And no soul perceives what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul perceives in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted

53:32.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَجۡتَنِبُونَ كَبَٰٓئِرَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّمَمَۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَٰسِعُ ٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِۚ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِكُمۡ إِذۡ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِذۡ أَنتُمۡ أَجِنَّةࣱ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمۡۖ فَلَا تُزَكُّوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡۖ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰٓ
53:32.en: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, only [committing] slight ones. Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness. He was most knowing of you when He produced you from the earth and when you were fetuses in the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim yourselves to be pure; He is most knowing of who fears Him

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And [mention, O Muhammad], when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority." They said, "Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we declare Your praise and sanctify You?" Allah said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know

2:31.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِي بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:31.en: And He taught Adam the names - all of them. Then He showed them to the angels and said, "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful

2:32.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلۡمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمۡتَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
2:32.en: They said, "Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, it is You who is the Knowing, the Wise

96:1.en: Recite in the name of your Lord who created

40:7.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَحۡمِلُونَ ٱلۡعَرۡشَ وَمَنۡ حَوۡلَهُۥ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَيُؤۡمِنُونَ بِهِۦ وَيَسۡتَغۡفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْۖ رَبَّنَا وَسِعۡتَ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲ رَّحۡمَةࣰ وَعِلۡمࣰ ا فَٱغۡفِرۡ لِلَّذِينَ تَابُواْ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ سَبِيلَكَ وَقِهِمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
40:7.en: Those [angels] who carry the Throne and those around it exalt [Allah] with praise of their Lord and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who have believed, [saying], "Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire

34:2.ar: يَعۡلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا يَخۡرُجُ مِنۡهَا وَمَا يَنزِلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا يَعۡرُجُ فِيهَاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلرَّحِيمُ ٱلۡغَفُورُ
34:2.en: He knows what penetrates into the earth and what emerges from it and what descends from the heaven and what ascends therein. And He is the Merciful, the Forgiving

18:65.ar: فَوَجَدَا عَبۡدࣰ ا مِّنۡ عِبَادِنَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّنۡ عِندِنَا وَعَلَّمۡنَٰهُ مِن لَّدُنَّا عِلۡمࣰ ا
18:65.en: And they found a servant from among Our servants to whom we had given mercy from us and had taught him from Us a [certain] knowledge

28:69.ar: وَرَبُّكَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا تُكِنُّ صُدُورُهُمۡ وَمَا يُعۡلِنُونَ
28:69.en: And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare

28:70.ar: وَهُوَ ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۖ لَهُ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ فِي ٱلۡأُولَىٰ وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۖ وَلَهُ ٱلۡحُكۡمُ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
28:70.en: And He is Allah; there is no deity except Him. To Him is [due all] praise in the first [life] and the Hereafter. And His is the [final] decision, and to Him you will be returned

28:71.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ سَرۡمَدًا إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ مَنۡ إِلَٰهٌ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِ يَأۡتِيكُم بِضِيَآءٍۚ أَفَلَا تَسۡمَعُونَ
28:71.en: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the night continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you light? Then will you not hear

28:72.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلنَّهَارَ سَرۡمَدًا إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ مَنۡ إِلَٰهٌ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِ يَأۡتِيكُم بِلَيۡلࣲ تَسۡكُنُونَ فِيهِۚ أَفَلَا تُبۡصِرُونَ
28:72.en: Say, "Have you considered: if Allah should make for you the day continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allah could bring you a night in which you may rest? Then will you not see

28:73.ar: وَمِن رَّحۡمَتِهِۦ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ لِتَسۡكُنُواْ فِيهِ وَلِتَبۡتَغُواْ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
28:73.en: And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and [by day] seek from His bounty and [that] perhaps you will be grateful

3:7.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِنۡهُ ءَايَٰتࣱ مُّحۡكَمَٰتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَٰبِهَٰتࣱۖ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡ زَيۡغࣱ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَٰبَهَ مِنۡهُ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةِ وَٱبۡتِغَآءَ تَأۡوِيلِهِۦۖ وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ تَأۡوِيلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُۗ وَٱلرَّٰسِخُونَ فِي ٱلۡعِلۡمِ يَقُولُونَ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ كُلࣱّ مِّنۡ عِندِ رَبِّنَاۗ وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّآ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
3:7.en: It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book; in it are verses [that are] precise - they are the foundation of the Book - and others unspecific. As for those in whose hearts is deviation [from truth], they will follow that of it which is unspecific, seeking discord and seeking an interpretation [suitable to them]. And no one knows its [true] interpretation except Allah. But those firm in knowledge say, "We believe in it. All [of it] is from our Lord." And no one will be reminded except those of understanding

3:8.ar: رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغۡ قُلُوبَنَا بَعۡدَ إِذۡ هَدَيۡتَنَا وَهَبۡ لَنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحۡمَةًۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡوَهَّابُ
3:8.en: [Who say], "Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower

35:28.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَٱلدَّوَآبِّ وَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ مُخۡتَلِفٌ أَلۡوَٰنُهُۥ كَذَٰلِكَۗ إِنَّمَا يَخۡشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِ ٱلۡعُلَمَٰٓؤُاْۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ غَفُورٌ
35:28.en: And among people and moving creatures and grazing livestock are various colors similarly. Only those fear Allah, from among His servants, who have knowledge. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Forgiving

mshxcXvBTeI.speaker: adnan
mshxcXvBTeI.speaker_note: Glorious Names series in his voice; quotes what his teacher used to tell him
mshxcXvBTeI.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Alim (The All-Knowing)
mshxcXvBTeI.one_line: Al-Alim: knowledge paired with wisdom and mercy, foreknowledge without compulsion, knowledge as strength and ignorance as the enemy, and becoming lifelong learners.
mshxcXvBTeI.summary: Al-Alim, an umbrella name appearing about 170 times, is one he says reason reaches even without revelation. It most often pairs with Al-Hakim, reassuring us that infinite knowledge is used wisely. He reads the verses on the keys of the unseen, the five things only Allah knows, and the command not to claim purity since Allah knows us from the womb. In the creation of Adam, the angels' objection turned to praise once Adam articulated the names, because they saw a new capacity to process, connect and build on knowledge; hence Allah taught bayan and the first revelation was Read, meaning to comprehend. He then draws four points. Allah encompasses all things with mercy and knowledge, and knowledge without mercy is catastrophic, from bombs to exploitation. His knowledge of the future does not compel it, since knowing is not an impactful attribute and Allah is outside the time He created; a god who could be surprised could be beaten. Knowledge is strength, and endless learning may be the greatest joy of Jannah, though schooling conditions people to find it dull. Ignorance is the ultimate enemy, turning power into oppression and religion into extremism. He urges people to become lifelong seekers of knowledge and to spread it, since rulers keep populations distracted and uninformed.

outline.heading: An umbrella name, 170 times in the Quran
outline.gist: Al-Alim is extremely general, gathering many narrower names, and appears far more often than the names covered earlier.

outline.heading: A name reason reaches on its own
outline.gist: Omniscience follows naturally from the idea of God; it appears as Alim, Allam al-Ghuyub and Knower of the unseen and seen.

outline.heading: Paired with many names, most of all Al-Hakim
outline.gist: Al-Alim accompanies over twelve names to clarify them, and most often appears with the All-Wise.

outline.heading: Knowledge guided by wisdom
outline.gist: Knowledge can harm unless joined to wisdom, so pairing it with Al-Hakim reassures us it is used for good.

outline.heading: The keys of the unseen
outline.gist: Not a leaf falls nor a seed lies in the earth's darkness, wet or dry, except that He knows it.

outline.heading: The five things only Allah knows
outline.gist: Knowledge of the Hour, rain, what is in wombs, what one will earn tomorrow and where one will die.

outline.heading: Do not claim purity for yourselves
outline.gist: He knew you from the earth and the womb, so do not boast of goodness; He knows who has taqwa.

outline.heading: The Prophet's dua describing Allah's knowledge
outline.gist: He knows the weight of mountains, the water in the seas, every leaf and raindrop, and what lies at the base of every mountain.

outline.heading: Adam: the angels object, Allah teaches the names
outline.gist: The angels feared another corrupting creature; Allah said He knows what they do not and taught Adam the names.

outline.heading: The angels' reaction changes
outline.gist: The angels, free of envy or agenda, praised Allah once Adam spoke, recognising knowledge only comes from Him.

outline.heading: Adam's unique potential to learn
outline.gist: Adam could process information, connect dots and build conclusions, something the angels had never seen.

outline.heading: He taught the Quran and taught man bayan
outline.gist: The ability to articulate lets knowledge pass to others who never experienced it, which is the basis of learning.

outline.heading: Iqra: read as comprehend
outline.gist: The first revealed command means to understand and read situations between the lines, not only to recite.

outline.heading: First point: encompassing all with mercy and knowledge
outline.gist: The angels' prayer says Allah encompasses everything with mercy and knowledge, attributes that reach all things equally, unlike provision or power.

outline.heading: Knowledge always beside mercy
outline.gist: Examples where knowledge and mercy appear together, including Khidr, given mercy and then knowledge.

outline.heading: Knowledge without mercy is catastrophic
outline.gist: The firmly grounded in knowledge ask for mercy, because knowledge without it builds bombs, exploits people and ruins the environment.

outline.heading: Second point: foreknowledge is not compulsion
outline.gist: His will and His knowledge are distinct; knowing something does not affect its existence, so His knowing the future does not force it.

outline.heading: Allah is outside time
outline.gist: Humans predict only what is programmed, but Allah created time and speaks of past and future alike, so He knows our free choices.

outline.heading: What came before Allah is a meaningless question
outline.gist: Before and after are features of created time, so they do not apply to Him.

outline.heading: A god who can be surprised can be beaten
outline.gist: Omniscience is part of what it means to be God, and it leaves our freedom of choice intact.

outline.heading: Third point: knowledge is strength, and the joy of Jannah
outline.gist: His teacher said the greatest joy of Paradise is access to Allah's infinite knowledge; the brain delights in learning more than in physical pleasures.

outline.heading: Schooling made us find knowledge dull
outline.gist: Conditioned to see learning as forced and boring, people step away from the most beautiful thing they have.

outline.heading: Fourth point: ignorance is the ultimate enemy
outline.gist: Ignorance with health breeds bullying, with wealth waste, with religion extremism, with power oppression; hence the pre-Islamic era is named after it.

outline.heading: Living the name: seek knowledge; scholar over worshipper
outline.gist: Be a lifelong learner; the scholar's superiority over the worshipper is like the Prophet's over the least of Muslims.

outline.heading: A path to Jannah made easy
outline.gist: Allah eases the way to Paradise for one who seeks knowledge, who has understood what truly matters.

outline.heading: The inheritance of the prophets and true reverence
outline.gist: Creatures of the sea seek forgiveness for the student, prophets left knowledge not money, and those who know truly revere Allah.

outline.heading: Living the name: spread knowledge
outline.gist: Raising the ummah's baseline of religious and academic knowledge is how it will recover.

outline.heading: Rulers keep people distracted and ignorant
outline.gist: Entertainment and distraction keep populations from asking questions and uncovering corruption.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Al-Alim, its pairings with other names and the Quranic scope of His knowledge.

themes.label: Seeking knowledge, learning and scholars
themes.note: Adam's unique capacity to learn, bayan, and Iqra as comprehension.

themes.label: Seeking knowledge, learning and scholars
themes.note: Knowledge as strength and joy, ignorance as the enemy, and the call to seek and spread knowledge.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: Allah's knowledge always accompanies His mercy; knowledge without mercy is destructive.

themes.label: Divine decree, foreknowledge and free will
themes.note: Allah's knowledge of the future does not compel it because He is outside time.

themes.label: Education, schools and learning disorders
themes.note: Schooling conditions people to find knowledge boring.

themes.label: Extremism, bad religiosity and distorted practice
themes.note: Ignorance combined with religion produces extremism.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions
themes.note: Rulers keep people uninformed and distracted to preserve the status quo.

quran.point: The keys of the unseen are with Him; not a leaf falls but He knows it
The five matters of the unseen known only to Allah
He knew you from the earth and in the womb, so do not claim purity
Allah announces a khalifah, teaches Adam the names, and the angels confess their limited knowledge
He taught the Quran, created man and taught him articulate speech
Read: the first revealed command, meaning to comprehend
Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge
He knows what enters the earth and what comes from it, what descends from the sky and ascends
Khidr was given mercy and taught knowledge, mercy mentioned first
He knows what chests conceal; from His mercy He made night and day
Those firm in knowledge ask for mercy from Him
Only those with knowledge truly fear Allah

hadith.gist: The Prophet's dua to the One whom eyes do not see: He knows the weight of mountains, the measure of seas, every leaf and raindrop, and no heaven or earth conceals another from Him
The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like my superiority over the least of you
Whoever takes a path seeking knowledge, Allah makes easy for him a path to Paradise, and the angels lower their wings for the student
Even the fish in the sea seek forgiveness for the seeker of knowledge; the prophets left no money, only knowledge, and whoever takes it takes an abundant share

maxims: Knowledge without mercy is catastrophic
Knowing something does not make it happen
Anything that can be surprised can be beaten
Ignorance is the ultimate enemy
Knowledge is strength

stories.who: The creation of Adam and the angels
stories.point: Humanity's distinction is its capacity to learn, process and articulate knowledge

stories.who: His teacher on the joy of Jannah
stories.point: The greatest delight of Paradise is endless access to Allah's knowledge

contemporary: Weapons of mass killing as knowledge without mercy
Schooling that makes learning dull
Rulers using entertainment and sports to keep people distracted
takeaways: Become a lifelong seeker of knowledge, both religious and academic
Pair whatever knowledge you gain with mercy
Do not claim goodness for yourself; Allah knows who has taqwa
Teach and spread what you know to raise the ummah's baseline
Hold to free choice while trusting Allah's complete knowledge

2:117.ar: بَدِيعُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَإِذَا قَضَىٰٓ أَمۡرࣰ ا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
2:117.en: Originator of the heavens and the earth. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is

6:101.ar: بَدِيعُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لَهُۥ وَلَدࣱ وَلَمۡ تَكُن لَّهُۥ صَٰحِبَةࣱۖ وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
6:101.en: [He is] Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He does not have a companion and He created all things? And He is, of all things, Knowing

13:2.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي رَفَعَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ بِغَيۡرِ عَمَدࣲ تَرَوۡنَهَاۖ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَۖ كُلࣱّ يَجۡرِي لِأَجَلࣲ مُّسَمࣰّ ىۚ يُدَبِّرُ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ يُفَصِّلُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُم بِلِقَآءِ رَبِّكُمۡ تُوقِنُونَ
13:2.en: It is Allah who erected the heavens without pillars that you [can] see; then He established Himself above the Throne and made subject the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. He arranges [each] matter; He details the signs that you may, of the meeting with your Lord, be certain

13:3.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي مَدَّ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَٰسِيَ وَأَنۡهَٰرࣰ اۖ وَمِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ جَعَلَ فِيهَا زَوۡجَيۡنِ ٱثۡنَيۡنِۖ يُغۡشِي ٱلَّيۡلَ ٱلنَّهَارَۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
13:3.en: And it is He who spread the earth and placed therein firmly set mountains and rivers; and from all of the fruits He made therein two mates; He causes the night to cover the day. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought

13:4.ar: وَفِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ قِطَعࣱ مُّتَجَٰوِرَٰتࣱ وَجَنَّٰتࣱ مِّنۡ أَعۡنَٰبࣲ وَزَرۡعࣱ وَنَخِيلࣱ صِنۡوَانࣱ وَغَيۡرُ صِنۡوَانࣲ يُسۡقَىٰ بِمَآءࣲ وَٰحِدࣲ وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعۡضَهَا عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ فِي ٱلۡأُكُلِۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
13:4.en: And within the land are neighboring plots and gardens of grapevines and crops and palm trees, [growing] several from a root or otherwise, watered with one water; but We make some of them exceed others in [quality of] fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason

25:45.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيۡفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ لَجَعَلَهُۥ سَاكِنࣰ ا ثُمَّ جَعَلۡنَا ٱلشَّمۡسَ عَلَيۡهِ دَلِيلࣰ ا
25:45.en: Have you not considered your Lord - how He extends the shadow, and if He willed, He could have made it stationary? Then We made the sun for it an indication

25:46.ar: ثُمَّ قَبَضۡنَٰهُ إِلَيۡنَا قَبۡضࣰ ا يَسِيرࣰ ا
25:46.en: Then We hold it in hand for a brief grasp

25:47.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ لِبَاسࣰ ا وَٱلنَّوۡمَ سُبَاتࣰ ا وَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ نُشُورࣰ ا
25:47.en: And it is He who has made the night for you as clothing and sleep [a means for] rest and has made the day a resurrection

25:48.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَرۡسَلَ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ بُشۡرَۢا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡ رَحۡمَتِهِۦۚ وَأَنزَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ طَهُورࣰ ا
25:48.en: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy, and We send down from the sky pure water

25:49.ar: لِّنُحۡـِۧيَ بِهِۦ بَلۡدَةࣰ مَّيۡتࣰ ا وَنُسۡقِيَهُۥ مِمَّا خَلَقۡنَآ أَنۡعَٰمࣰ ا وَأَنَاسِيَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا
25:49.en: That We may bring to life thereby a dead land and give it as drink to those We created of numerous livestock and men

16:3.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ تَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
16:3.en: He created the heavens and earth in truth. High is He above what they associate with Him

16:4.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ مِن نُّطۡفَةࣲ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
16:4.en: He created man from a sperm-drop; then at once, he is a clear adversary

16:5.ar: وَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمَ خَلَقَهَاۖ لَكُمۡ فِيهَا دِفۡءࣱ وَمَنَٰفِعُ وَمِنۡهَا تَأۡكُلُونَ
16:5.en: And the grazing livestock He has created for you; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits, and from them you eat

16:6.ar: وَلَكُمۡ فِيهَا جَمَالٌ حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ وَحِينَ تَسۡرَحُونَ
16:6.en: And for you in them is [the enjoyment of] beauty when you bring them in [for the evening] and when you send them out [to pasture]

16:7.ar: وَتَحۡمِلُ أَثۡقَالَكُمۡ إِلَىٰ بَلَدࣲ لَّمۡ تَكُونُواْ بَٰلِغِيهِ إِلَّا بِشِقِّ ٱلۡأَنفُسِۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكُمۡ لَرَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
16:7.en: And they carry your loads to a land you could not have reached except with difficulty to yourselves. Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful

16:8.ar: وَٱلۡخَيۡلَ وَٱلۡبِغَالَ وَٱلۡحَمِيرَ لِتَرۡكَبُوهَا وَزِينَةࣰۚ وَيَخۡلُقُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
16:8.en: And [He created] the horses, mules and donkeys for you to ride and [as] adornment. And He creates that which you do not know

16:9.ar: وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ قَصۡدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَمِنۡهَا جَآئِرࣱۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ لَهَدَىٰكُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ
16:9.en: And upon Allah is the direction of the [right] way, and among the various paths are those deviating. And if He willed, He could have guided you all

16:10.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰۖ لَّكُم مِّنۡهُ شَرَابࣱ وَمِنۡهُ شَجَرࣱ فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ
16:10.en: It is He who sends down rain from the sky; from it is drink and from it is foliage in which you pasture [animals]

16:11.ar: يُنۢبِتُ لَكُم بِهِ ٱلزَّرۡعَ وَٱلزَّيۡتُونَ وَٱلنَّخِيلَ وَٱلۡأَعۡنَٰبَ وَمِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَةࣰ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
16:11.en: He causes to grow for you thereby the crops, olives, palm trees, grapevines, and from all the fruits. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought

16:12.ar: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَۖ وَٱلنُّجُومُ مُسَخَّرَٰتُۢ بِأَمۡرِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
16:12.en: And He has subjected for you the night and day and the sun and moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason

2:26.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَسۡتَحۡيِۦٓ أَن يَضۡرِبَ مَثَلࣰ ا مَّا بَعُوضَةࣰ فَمَا فَوۡقَهَاۚ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ فَيَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡۖ وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَيَقُولُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلࣰ اۘ يُضِلُّ بِهِۦ كَثِيرࣰ ا وَيَهۡدِي بِهِۦ كَثِيرࣰ اۚ وَمَا يُضِلُّ بِهِۦٓ إِلَّا ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
2:26.en: Indeed, Allah is not timid to present an example - that of a mosquito or what is smaller than it. And those who have believed know that it is the truth from their Lord. But as for those who disbelieve, they say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?" He misleads many thereby and guides many thereby. And He misleads not except the defiantly disobedient

50:6.ar: أَفَلَمۡ يَنظُرُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَوۡقَهُمۡ كَيۡفَ بَنَيۡنَٰهَا وَزَيَّنَّٰهَا وَمَا لَهَا مِن فُرُوجࣲ‏
50:6.en: Have they not looked at the heaven above them - how We structured it and adorned it and [how] it has no rifts

50:7.ar: وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ مَدَدۡنَٰهَا وَأَلۡقَيۡنَا فِيهَا رَوَٰسِيَ وَأَنۢبَتۡنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوۡجِۭ بَهِيجࣲ‏
50:7.en: And the earth - We spread it out and cast therein firmly set mountains and made grow therein [something] of every beautiful kind

50:8.en: Giving insight and a reminder for every servant who turns [to Allah]

6:99.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا بِهِۦ نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا مِنۡهُ خَضِرࣰ ا نُّخۡرِجُ مِنۡهُ حَبࣰّ ا مُّتَرَاكِبࣰ ا وَمِنَ ٱلنَّخۡلِ مِن طَلۡعِهَا قِنۡوَانࣱ دَانِيَةࣱ وَجَنَّٰتࣲ مِّنۡ أَعۡنَابࣲ وَٱلزَّيۡتُونَ وَٱلرُّمَّانَ مُشۡتَبِهࣰ ا وَغَيۡرَ مُتَشَٰبِهٍۗ ٱنظُرُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ ثَمَرِهِۦٓ إِذَآ أَثۡمَرَ وَيَنۡعِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكُمۡ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
6:99.en: And it is He who sends down rain from the sky, and We produce thereby the growth of all things. We produce from it greenery from which We produce grains arranged in layers. And from the palm trees - of its emerging fruit are clusters hanging low. And [We produce] gardens of grapevines and olives and pomegranates, similar yet varied. Look at [each of] its fruit when it yields and [at] its ripening. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe

12:18.ar: وَجَآءُو عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِۦ بِدَمࣲ كَذِبࣲۚ قَالَ بَلۡ سَوَّلَتۡ لَكُمۡ أَنفُسُكُمۡ أَمۡرࣰ اۖ فَصَبۡرࣱ جَمِيلࣱۖ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُسۡتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ
12:18.en: And they brought upon his shirt false blood. [Jacob] said, "Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. And Allah is the one sought for help against that which you describe

33:28.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لِّأَزۡوَٰجِكَ إِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدۡنَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَزِينَتَهَا فَتَعَالَيۡنَ أُمَتِّعۡكُنَّ وَأُسَرِّحۡكُنَّ سَرَاحࣰ ا جَمِيلࣰ ا
33:28.en: O Prophet, say to your wives, "If you should desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and give you a gracious release

15:85.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَآ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّۗ وَإِنَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ لَأٓتِيَةࣱۖ فَٱصۡفَحِ ٱلصَّفۡحَ ٱلۡجَمِيلَ
15:85.en: And We have not created the heavens and earth and that between them except in truth. And indeed, the Hour is coming; so forgive with gracious forgiveness

67:3.ar: ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبۡعَ سَمَٰوَٰتࣲ طِبَاقࣰ اۖ مَّا تَرَىٰ فِي خَلۡقِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ مِن تَفَٰوُتࣲۖ فَٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ هَلۡ تَرَىٰ مِن فُطُورࣲ‏
67:3.en: [And] who created seven heavens in layers. You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency. So return [your] vision [to the sky]; do you see any breaks

67:4.ar: ثُمَّ ٱرۡجِعِ ٱلۡبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيۡنِ يَنقَلِبۡ إِلَيۡكَ ٱلۡبَصَرُ خَاسِئࣰ ا وَهُوَ حَسِيرࣱ‏
67:4.en: Then return [your] vision twice again. [Your] vision will return to you humbled while it is fatigued

67:5.ar: وَلَقَدۡ زَيَّنَّا ٱلسَّمَآءَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا بِمَصَٰبِيحَ وَجَعَلۡنَٰهَا رُجُومࣰ ا لِّلشَّيَٰطِينِۖ وَأَعۡتَدۡنَا لَهُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
67:5.en: And We have certainly beautified the nearest heaven with stars and have made [from] them what is thrown at the devils and have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze

35:1.ar: ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ فَاطِرِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَاعِلِ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ رُسُلًا أُوْلِيٓ أَجۡنِحَةࣲ مَّثۡنَىٰ وَثُلَٰثَ وَرُبَٰعَۚ يَزِيدُ فِي ٱلۡخَلۡقِ مَا يَشَآءُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
35:1.en: [All] praise is [due] to Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, [who] made the angels messengers having wings, two or three or four. He increases in creation what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent

w-nyJFcGYlw.speaker: adnan
w-nyJFcGYlw.speaker_note: Ramadan morning Names of Allah series in his voice; personal anecdote about a residency interview in Halifax
w-nyJFcGYlw.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Badi' (The Innovator)
w-nyJFcGYlw.one_line: Al-Badi', the One who originated all creation without precedent, and how it calls us to notice beauty and act beautifully.
w-nyJFcGYlw.summary: Continuing the names of creation, he presents Al-Badi' as the One who invented everything with no previous example. Human creativity, however brilliant, always copies or recombines patterns Allah already made, and our first attempts are rarely good, while Allah needed no model or practice. Most of the talk walks through Quranic passages that list the beauty of creation: the raised heavens, the earth's gardens irrigated by one water yet differing in taste, the moving shade, livestock and horses, the sea and stars. He argues that witnessing this beauty is one of the great gifts of being alive, available every sunrise and the reason people love to travel, and that even the smallest creatures the Quraysh mocked reveal astonishing detail. From the hadith that Allah is beautiful and loves beauty, he extends beauty from appearance to conduct: beautiful patience, a beautiful divorce, forgiving without a last humiliating word, and parting ways with partners or friends gracefully. He ends with two ways to live the name: channel creativity into serving people rather than inventing new rituals or forbidding what Allah allowed, and pause to appreciate the colours and sounds of the world as the Prophet did, staying connected to the creation around us.

outline.heading: Al-Badi' within the names of creation
outline.gist: He places the name within his twelve categories of Allah's names and describes it as a name about beauty.

outline.heading: Meaning: inventing with no previous example
outline.gist: Al-Badi' appears twice in the Quran, as Originator of the heavens and earth who only says 'be'; it means creating creatively without any precedent.

outline.heading: All human invention is imitation
outline.gist: Planes, helicopters and submarines copy designs Allah made; the most creative people recombine His patterns, which should deepen appreciation of His magnificence.

outline.heading: No first drafts for Allah
outline.gist: Human first attempts are usually poor and need practice, but Allah innovated everything without coaching or repeated attempts.

outline.heading: Surat al-Ra'd: heavens without pillars, gardens of one water
outline.gist: Raised skies, subjected sun and moon, mountains and rivers, and neighbouring plots watered alike yet differing in taste, as signs for those who think.

outline.heading: Surat al-Furqan: shade, night, rest and rain
outline.gist: The shade moved by the sun, night for rest, day for living, and winds and rain that revive dead land.

outline.heading: Surat an-Nahl: livestock, horses, water, the sea and stars
outline.gist: A long passage on blessings that carry warmth, food, beauty and transport, ending with the sea, mountains, paths and stars made to serve people.

outline.heading: His innovation is endless
outline.gist: If you counted Allah's blessings you could never finish; the more we look and search, the more of His invention we find.

outline.heading: Witnessing beauty is a gift of being alive
outline.gist: Step outside and look at the colours of the dawn horizon; His creation is always at your fingertips and never grows boring.

outline.heading: Travel and the first sight of the ocean
outline.gist: People love travel because they see new parts of creation; he recalls being stunned by the Atlantic in Halifax and saying subhanallah beside his aunt.

outline.heading: The parable of the mosquito and the insect surahs
outline.gist: The Quraysh mocked a Lord who speaks of ants, spiders and bees; today the systems inside tiny creatures should increase our awe of His invention.

outline.heading: Look at the sky, the earth and the ripening fruit
outline.gist: Verses on a flawless adorned sky and gardens as insight for every returning heart, and the command to watch fruit as it forms and ripens.

outline.heading: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty
outline.gist: The context of trailing garments as a show of status and arrogance, and the companions' question about fine clothes and shoes; Allah loves to see His blessing on His servant.

outline.heading: Al-Badi' as the producer of beauty: behave beautifully
outline.gist: Beautiful is a description rather than a name, but part of this name; Allah asks for beautiful appearance and beautiful conduct.

outline.heading: Beautiful patience
outline.gist: Ya'qub's patience shows one can persevere while staying optimistic and working toward a goal instead of being grumpy and broken.

outline.heading: Even divorce must be beautiful
outline.gist: The Quran asks for a beautiful release in separation, not only in marriage.

outline.heading: Forgive beautifully
outline.gist: Do not deliver one last piece of your mind before forgiving; forgive without humiliating the other person.

outline.heading: Parting ways beautifully
outline.gist: When friends or partners cannot work together, part on that matter without ending the friendship.

outline.heading: Surat al-Mulk: look again for a flaw
outline.gist: The seven heavens show no defect however many times you look; the sky is adorned with lamps.

outline.heading: Surat Fatir: angels with wings
outline.gist: The Originator released creation and made angels messengers with wings, adding to creation as He wills because there is beauty in it.

outline.heading: The Prophet sees Jibril in his true form
outline.gist: Jibril filling the horizon with hundreds of wings, and at the Ascension appearing like a worn cloth out of reverence for Allah.

outline.heading: Living the name: innovate in service, not in religion
outline.gist: Be creative in making people's lives easier, but do not invent rituals, self-harm as worship, or forbid the adornments Allah permitted.

outline.heading: Living the name: appreciate the beauty around you
outline.gist: Children hearing for the first time, birdsong, and the Muslim's rituals tied to sun, moon, rain and thunder; the Prophet was deeply connected to the world around him.

themes.note: Al-Badi' as originating creation without precedent and as the producer of beauty.

themes.label: Beauty: noticing it and producing it
themes.note: The Quran repeatedly tells people to look at the beauty of creation; seeing it is one of the great gifts of life.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: Forgive without a final humiliating word.

themes.label: Extremism, bad religiosity and distorted practice
themes.note: Creativity must not invent new rituals, self-harm or bans on what Allah made lawful.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: His strong connection to and appreciation of the world around him.

KKEaKkRj7Pk.speaker_note: Glorious Names series in his voice; refers to verses he recited in the prayer the night before
KKEaKkRj7Pk.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Qahhar (The Subduer)
KKEaKkRj7Pk.one_line: Al-Qahhar: a name we must not imitate, how Allah subdues all creation, the three ways we are compelled, and why the only thing to subdue is the self.
KKEaKkRj7Pk.summary: Opening the category of correctional control, he explains that Al-Qahhar is unlike names we are asked to emulate: compelling and overpowering belong to Allah alone and the name exists to fill hearts with reverence and turn people from sin. It appears paired only with Al-Wahid because nothing stands beside it. He reads the verses: the Day the earth is replaced and all stand exposed before the One, the Subduer; Yusuf choosing this name when speaking to fellow prisoners, reminding them that the true subduer is not the jailer; the verses that reject partners and the notion of a son; and the angels recording until death. He shows the name in creation, the heavens coming willingly, sun and moon in fixed orbits, and in Allah reversing the nature of things, from water that will burn to the birds against the army of the elephant, the knife that would not cut Isma'il, the fire that would not burn Ibrahim, and Namrud's death by a mosquito. Humans are compelled in three ways: by death, by being given free will that ends on Judgment Day, and by eventual worship that will only count if done now. Islam itself means submission, as in Ibrahim's test and the rites of Hajj. He asks for khashyah, for abandoning the struggle for power over others, and for subduing one's own nafs.

outline.heading: Names of correctional control
outline.gist: This category covers how Allah brings people back from sin and indifference; he chooses Al-Qahhar from it.

outline.heading: A name we must not emulate
outline.gist: Unlike many names we are encouraged to embody, this one exists to instil reverence and fear that move people to leave sin.

outline.heading: Meaning: to subdue, compel and overpower
outline.gist: These words do not fit a servant's conduct; compelling is Allah's role, not ours.

outline.heading: The Day the earth is changed
outline.gist: Everything will be transformed and every person exposed before Allah, the One, the Subduer.

outline.heading: Paired only with Al-Wahid
outline.gist: No other name stands beside it, and on that Day the call will be: whose is the kingdom today? Allah's, the One, the Subduer.

outline.heading: Yusuf in prison: the true Subduer
outline.gist: Unjustly jailed after being thrown in a well, Yusuf reminded his fellow inmates that Allah, not their captors, is the One who subdues all.

outline.heading: Allah created everything; the Prophet only warns
outline.gist: Partners own no harm or benefit; Allah is Creator of all, the One, the Subduer, and no one can claim they were not warned.

outline.heading: Had He wanted a son
outline.gist: The bond between Creator and creation is closer than father and son, since all of us belongs to Him; He is exalted above taking a child.

outline.heading: Subduer over His servants: angels and death
outline.gist: He sends recording angels until death takes the soul, and returns everyone to Him for swift judgment.

outline.heading: The cosmos subdued
outline.gist: The heavens and earth came willingly at His command; sun and moon run their decreed orbits without overtaking one another.

outline.heading: Compelling things to their opposite
outline.gist: Water, the elixir of life, will be made to burn on the Last Day.

outline.heading: The people of the elephant
outline.gist: A few birds carrying pebbles destroyed an army's whole scheme.

outline.heading: The knife, the fire and the mosquito
outline.gist: The knife would not cut Isma'il, the fire would not burn Ibrahim, and Namrud was undone by a mosquito.

outline.heading: First compulsion: death
outline.gist: No one escapes death; it is pure compulsion without oppression, and accepting it early helps one live well.

outline.heading: Second compulsion: the gift of free will
outline.gist: Everything follows its decreed course except humans, whose choice exists only because Allah willed it, and it is withdrawn on Judgment Day.

outline.heading: Third compulsion: everyone will worship
outline.gist: All will eventually pray, love and revere Him; the only question is whether now, when it counts, or after death, when nothing is recorded.

outline.heading: Islam means submission
outline.gist: Islam is surrender, a name taken from Ibrahim, who obeyed the command to sacrifice his son without seeing its wisdom.

outline.heading: Hajj rites as submission
outline.gist: Circling a stone house and throwing pebbles are done because Allah commanded them, whether or not we see the symbolism.

outline.heading: Living the name: khashyah
outline.gist: Reverence combines fear of fair punishment, magnification of His status, and love.

outline.heading: Living the name: do not compel others
outline.gist: Let go of the futile struggle for power; any power should defend the weak, and never coerce an orphan or anyone weaker.

outline.heading: Living the name: subdue your own nafs
outline.gist: The one thing you are meant to overpower is yourself; turning that force on others instead is the worst misuse.

themes.note: Abandon the struggle for power and never coerce the weak.
